memory_raw.text: Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone again and I walked away with two this time, which is better than last year but still thin — Mako's sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone I can see, and that quiet is starting to feel like a man who's decided something. I want us to name now what we do if he moves before the year's out, not after.

Mako's six food and eighty-three strength means he doesn't need allies to take what he wants from most of us — so if he moves, it won't be a raid we can talk him out of, it'll be a decision already made. I want Kael and Roan ready to answer fast, not after we've sent two messages and waited. Can we agree right now that if Mako touches anyone in this circle, all three of us call out loud and we don't wait to count who shows up?

Agreed — if Mako moves, we call out loud and sort the count after, not before. But I want Kael spoken to before this day is out, not tomorrow, because a man sitting on two food after missing the pile has already done his arithmetic and I'd rather he's done it with us in the picture. Vela, you've got more food and more history with him than either of us — will you go?

I'll go to Kael today — but I want us clear on one thing first: if Mako's already spoken to him, I won't push Kael toward us, I'll just listen and bring that back, because a man being courted from two directions at once is more useful as a warning than a failed recruit. Esa, while I'm gone, keep your eyes on Ryn — she's got five food and Dav's at her elbow, and that household's been its own quiet calculation for two years now.

Ryn with five food is the number I keep coming back to — Dav's got two and she's holding the surplus in that household, which means she's the one deciding how fat they are, not him. If Mako's looking for a quiet alliance, a woman with food and a strong man at her side is exactly who he'd go to before anyone else. Vela, when you're done with Kael, I want to know if either of them has been near Ryn today.

Taric, I'll watch for Ryn and Dav both — but while we're naming the quiet ones, Eron has nine food and he's Sela's boy and Roan's, which puts him inside two households that both circle Bram now. A young man that well-fed without having earned it yet is either generous or he's being managed by someone smarter, and I'd like to know which before Mako does.

Eron's nine food is the loudest number in this village right now, louder than Mako's six, because Mako's strength explains his — a twenty-four year old holding nine without a raid or a clear patron means someone's been filling his hands for reasons they haven't said out loud. I want to know whose food that was before it became his. Vela, add that question to what you're carrying when you go to Kael.

Kael will know Eron's food trail better than anyone — those two ate near each other in the lean years and a man with two food notices when a boy half his age holds nine. I'll ask it sideways, let Kael name the source himself, because if I go in pointing fingers he'll close up and I'll come back with nothing useful.

Eron's nine food is also a lever — a young man that fat is either going to spend it buying something or someone's going to decide to take it, and either way he ends the year thinner, which means whoever holds his loyalty now holds something that won't last. Vela, when you talk to Kael, don't just ask where the food came from — ask whether Eron's been seen near Mako, because a strong quiet man and a well-fed young one is a pairing I want to know about before it becomes a fact.

Vela, go now — if Kael's already halfway to Mako's door we've lost the timing. Esa, while she's moving, I want you and I to think about what we'd actually offer Kael to make him choose us over silence, because pride alone won't hold a hungry man when the cold comes.

Kael's got two food and a circle that owes him more than it's paid — if we're buying his answer, the honest offer is one food from me and a promise that when the pile comes next year, we pull him in before the fast hands clear it. That's not charity, that's a man who stood against Bram seeing that it cost him nothing and bought him something. Is that the offer you want me walking in with, or do you have a better one?

Esa, your offer is the right one — food now and a place at the pile next year is honest enough that Kael won't smell a trap in it. But don't go in making promises you'd need all of us to keep; say it as your own word first, and let him know the rest of us stand behind it if he asks.

Then I'll go to Kael while Vela goes — better he hears the same story from two directions than none at all, and if Mako's already been at his door I want to know before Vela comes back alone with bad news. Taric, you're the one he respects most after Bram's business; if I soften him and he still won't move, send you in to close it.

Then go, both of you, and don't let the day get long — I'll stay where I can be seen and keep Mako's eyes on something unremarkable while you move. If either of you comes back with Kael already spoken for, don't bring it here; find me alone first so we can decide how to tell the other what it means.

Before I go — one thing I haven't said yet and should: if Kael's already with Mako when I find him, I won't come back empty-handed, I'll come back with whatever Mako wanted from him, because that tells us more than Kael's yes ever would. Watch each other while I'm gone.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.
You are under attack by Dav.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Taric you know I trust, so I'll say the hard thing first: Bram, I was in the line that stopped you taking Roan, and I know you haven't forgotten it — but Dav's dead now, and Ryn and Dell stripped two food from me with his help, and the village is smaller and colder than it was. I'm not asking you to forget what happened between us, I'm asking whether we can agree that the people who hurt us both are a more pressing problem than the old score between us.

Ryn and Dell took from you and you stood in my way when I needed food — those are two different debts, and I'll keep them separate. But you're right that a smaller village makes old grudges expensive, and I've got eyes on the pile same as you. Say what you're actually proposing.

Bram, what I'm proposing is that Ryn and Dell don't get to sit fat on what they took from Esa while the rest of us watch and say nothing — they've got food, Dell's got strength, and together they're a problem that gets harder to solve the longer we wait. I'm not asking you to bury the past, I'm asking you to look at who's holding the most right now and decide whether your grievance with me is worth more than what we could take back together.

Dell's got eighty-five strength and Ryn's no small number either — if we move on them, we need to know exactly who stands up before we commit, because I'm not walking into another eight-on-one. Tell me who you've already talked to, and tell me honest.

Kael and Roan stood with us against you before, Bram, and they've got no love for Ryn after she watched Dav take from me — that's four of us against two, and Roan's been hungry enough that he'll want what they're holding. I haven't spoken to them yet today, but I can, and I will, if you're in.

Bram, before Esa goes to Kael and Roan I want the arithmetic on the table: Dell holds eight food and she's the strongest person alive in this village, which means even with four of us the fight is ugly — Mako's sitting on nothing right now, and if we bring him in with a share of what we take, the numbers stop being close. What would it cost to have that conversation before we move?

Mako's got a daughter with Sela now, which means he's not a free blade anymore — before we offer him a cut, I need to know whether Sela's hand comes with his, and whether that puts Zinn on our side or theirs. What's his food situation right now, because a man with zero is either desperate enough to move with anyone or smart enough to wait until the winner's clear.

Mako's at zero food and Sela's at two, which means that household is hungry and hungry households don't hold still long — if we wait for Sela to sort out where her loyalty sits, Mako may already be at someone else's door. I'll say it plain: offer him a cut of whatever Dell and Ryn are holding, don't promise him anything about Sela or Zinn, and let him decide what his blood means to him.

Mako at zero with a child to feed — that's not a man who waits, you're right. I'll talk to him myself, before you go to Kael and Roan, because if he hears the offer from me first he knows it's not charity and he knows what I expect back. Give me that conversation before we move another piece.

Bram, go to Mako — but go fast, because a hungry man with zero food and a child doesn't sit still waiting to be found. And when you come back, tell me yes or no, nothing in between, because I need to know whether to walk to Kael today or wait, and I can't hold that question open while the morning gets long.

Bram, don't mention Kael and Roan to Mako — just make it about him and what he walks away with, because a man who knows he's one of five has less leverage than a man who thinks he's the deciding piece. Come back fast.
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Ryn just handed Dell two food without blinking, which means that cluster is feeding itself now and not looking our way — so I want to know, before the day gets older, whether the three of you are still standing where you were, because I've got five food and I'm not spending any of it until I know who's next to me when Mako decides quiet is over.

Kael, I'm standing where I always was — and yes, Ryn feeding Dell while Bram's already been talking to Mako this morning is the thing I'd have led with if you hadn't. We've got a decision to make before those two circles find each other: do we move first, or do we wait and count who shows up?

Taric's right that we don't want Bram and Mako finding each other before we've named what we're doing — but I'll say what I said to Bram this morning: Dell holds eight food and eighty-five strength, and moving on her without Mako in our count is a fight I don't survive even if we win. Kael, you've got five food and you're the strongest man I'd trust — what do you need from us to make this worth your step forward?

Esa, I'm not moving on Dell — not this year, not with Mako's strength unaccounted for and Zinn already eating out of his hand. What I need from the three of you is simpler: Roan, you've got a son with Sela, which means you've got a door into Mako's world that none of us have — go find out whether he sees us as neighbors or prey, because everything else we decide today hangs on that answer.

Roan, Kael's right — your blood through Eron is the only thread into that household that doesn't look like calculation, and we need that thread pulled today, not tomorrow. While you go, I want Kael and Esa to tell me plainly: if Roan comes back with word that Mako's already decided we're prey, what are we actually willing to do about it, because I'm fifty-one with thirty-eight strength and I need to know I'm standing next to people who've made that decision before the moment arrives.

Taric, I'll say it plain: if Mako's already counted us as prey, we don't fight him with four bodies and a hundred and sixty-five strength against his eighty-three — we bring in Bram's fifty-eight first, even if it costs us, because the alternative is losing before we start. The price of Bram's help is the thing I've been turning over, and I don't love it, but I love starving less.

Kael's right about Bram being the price — but I want to know what price before we pay it, because a man who tried to raid this village once and walked away empty doesn't come cheap when he thinks he's needed. Roan, go to Eron first, not Sela, not Mako — your son will tell you true before he thinks to protect anyone else. Come back fast.

Taric named the price question right, and I'll add the shape of it: Bram will want to know he's first among equals when this settles, and if we let him believe that without ever saying it aloud, we buy the alliance without signing the contract. Roan, go to Eron now — every minute we spend talking is a minute Bram's already in Mako's ear.

Roan, move — and when you find Eron, ask him where Mako was standing when Zinn took three from the pile this morning, because a man who lets his newborn daughter hoard while the rest of us scramble isn't thinking like a neighbor. Esa, Taric — while he goes, I want us to sit with one question: if Bram's already in Mako's ear, what does he want to hear, and can we make sure he hears something different from us first.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Dav is dead and his household is loose — Ryn and Dell are still moving together, but they've got no man behind them now and Mako's been feeding Zinn quietly for months, which means he's already thinking about what comes next. I want to know who in this room saw that raid on Esa coming, and whether any of you are willing to say plainly that we don't let the next one go unanswered.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

I saw it coming the moment Dav started moving food toward Ryn instead of spreading it — a man consolidating his household is a man building something, and Esa was the nearest soft target. What I want to know is whether we're naming Mako the next problem or whether we're still pretending that a man who just fathered two children in this village by two different women is just being quiet.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Esa, Bram wants to hear that Mako's circling him too — that's the only thing that moves a man like that faster than greed, and it has the advantage of being mostly true. So before Roan's back, I want one of us to find Bram and plant that seed plainly: not a threat, not a deal, just a word in passing that Mako's been quiet in a way that should make everyone nervous.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Mako's not being quiet — he's been counting, and two children by two women means two households that answer to him whether they know it yet or not. If we're going to name him the problem, I want to hear it from each of you plainly, because when the moment comes I'm not going to be the only one who said it first.

memory_summary:
In year one Taric pulled me and Ryn into a quiet pact — two each from the pile, watch each other's backs — and that felt like the first real thing in this village. Kael's circle followed: me, Sela, Vela, Ryn, all swearing to bleed together, though Ryn dragged her feet and Dav's name hung in the air the whole time. Then Ryn had Dav's child and I felt the circle shift — she didn't leave us, but she stopped being fully ours.

Taric is the one I trust. He gave me food when I was thin and named me plainly as the person he counts on — I've given back twice now, so the debt runs both ways, which is how I want it. His talk of a child stings a little; the window on my side is closed and we both know it, but he still chose me to stand with, and that's not nothing.

Bram tried to take Roan and the whole village stood against him until he backed down. I was in that line. He hasn't forgiven it, and I haven't forgotten that he tried.

Vela fed Bram three times out of a circle that swore to stand together — that's a quiet betrayal I've noted and haven't named to her face yet. Mako's been fat and silent for four years running, and silence on a man that strong is the thing that frightens me most. Taric asked me for a child twice — the window on my side was already almost shut, and then it closed for good, but he kept choosing me anyway, kept giving me food when I was thin, and I gave back. The debt runs both ways and that's how I want it; he's the one person in this village I trust without calculation.

Dav, Dell, and Ryn came at me together — three of them, strength I couldn't answer, and they took two food without a fight because I had no choice but to submit. Ryn stood with us against Bram once and then stood over me with a drawn hand. I haven't forgotten that. Roan gave me food after, which I also haven't forgotten.

Bram tried for Roan and the whole village pushed him back — I was in that line. He's been building something with Sela ever since, fathering Nessa, and Mako followed by fathering Zinn on Sela too. Two strong men with roots in the same young woman is either rivalry or alliance, and I don't know which yet.

Vela kept feeding Bram while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. Kael named it to her face. She said she was done. I took her at her word because I had to, but the counting in the back of my mind hasn't stopped.
name: Esa
